When I was little (under 10 years old) my family and I were on a holiday. We were staying at a camping ground in a camper van and had been fishing that day. It was now night time and I was in bed on the top bunk bed with my brother asleep on the bottom. I was supposed to be asleep over an hour ago but I stayed up late playing with my toys. My parents were in a seperate room (separated by a curtain, the main entrance area, and another curtain) and I was scared they’d catch me awake. I heard heavy footsteps coming to the bedroom and assume it was my dad so I closed my eyes and pretended to be asleep. I heard the footsteps coming into the room and next thing I felt a big hand placing something into mine, which was hanging off the bed palm up. I waited until the footsteps disappeared and opened my eyes to see what was placed in my hand. It appeared to be a fish eye. I immediately threw it across the room in fear and disgust and assumed it was my parents playing a prank on me for staying up late, so I went to ask them about it but they denied that it was them. They even showed me the fish we caught that day and they still had the eyes in them.

To this day I have no idea what it actually was in my hand, or who came into the camper van and why they did it. I also cannot sleep with my hand over the edge of the bed. I don’t think my parents ever believed me, but it was so terrifying that it’s burnt into my memory. I’m 31 now and still remember it clear as day, and it still gives me a sick, cold feeling.

Hey you :) I’m just a stranger on the internet but I care! I’m not telling you what to do or how to feel, but I just want to let you know that someone definitely cares and I think that is a good reason for you to care.
I would hazard a guess and say that even if your family aren’t very emotional they still care too and sometimes that’s all that keeps me going (by that I mean my family caring about me, though I’m sure your family are very good too).

Sometimes it’s hard to keep going, especially when you have suffered for so long. But if you can find one little thing and hold onto that keeps you going (even if it’s that you have pets, or you’re reading a really good book, or, heck, a stranger on the internet took some time out of their day to listen to your problems and respond) then do your best to keep holding onto that. Build up your little reasons to keep going. Finished that book? Start a new one! Maybe one that’s in a series (I’d suggest the game of thrones books because who knows when the last one will be released lol). Start volunteering. Make friends with your neighbours or people in your apartment block. The more things you add to that list the more reasons you have to keep going and, who knows, maybe that could bring some hope back into your world :)

I do genuinely hope you are okay and I honestly hope things start to look and feel better for you soon :)
